candidates.explanation: I could not read the files, so this diagnosis and the line numbers are estimates based on the usual layout of this boilerplate. resetPassword verifies the hash, sets the new password and saves the user. It appears not to revoke the user's existing sessions, for example with sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id }). The phone's session row therefore stays valid, and its refresh token can still be exchanged for new tokens after the reset.

If resetPassword does call session deletion, this method may be the fault. A wrong filter, or a delete that is never awaited or executed, would leave the user's sessions in place. The document-store repository has the same method and could share the problem. These line numbers are also estimates.

Refresh only checks that the session exists and that the hash matches. It does not check whether the password changed after the session was created. Without session revocation on reset, an old session can keep renewing tokens. Line numbers are estimates.

fix.description: In AuthService.resetPassword, after validating the hash and finding the user, call `await this.sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id })` before or after `usersService.update`. This removes every session for that user, so all devices are signed out. Also check that SessionService.deleteByUserId and the repository implementations filter on the user id and are awaited.

It appears not to revoke the user's existing sessions, for example with sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id }). The phone's session row therefore stays valid, and its refresh token can still be exchanged for new tokens after the reset.

If resetPassword does call session deletion, this method may be the fault. A wrong filter, or a delete that is never awaited or executed, would leave the user's sessions in place. The document-store repository has the same method and could share the problem. These line numbers are also estimates.

Refresh only checks that the session exists and that the hash matches. It does not check whether the password changed after the session was created. Without session revocation on reset, an old session can keep renewing tokens. Line numbers are estimates.

fix.description: In AuthService.resetPassword, after validating the hash and finding the user, call `await this.sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id })` before or after `usersService.update`. This removes every session for that user, so all devices are signed out. Also check that SessionService.deleteByUserId and the repository implementations filter on the user id and are awaited.
